item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.11
item.description:
Read this first: the solver's interior scheme has changed, and every number on every document with a pipe in it moves — tuned points most. A sweep now takes about 1.5× longer at the working 7 mm mesh. One key restores the previous scheme bit for bit (below).

A sharper solver. The interior scheme is now a fifth-order WENO reconstruction with a three-stage Runge–Kutta integrator, in place of MacCormack + the Davis TVD limiter. The old limiter clipped a little off every crest of a tuned wave on every pass — a loss that shrank only as the mesh was halved, and that took 7.9 % off the reference engine's 3200 rpm scavenging index at the working 7 mm mesh. The new scheme keeps resolved waves whole: at 7 mm the same point now sits 1.1 % from its converged value, the drone band's numerical attenuation falls from 0.0001 to 0.00005 dB/m, and the 800 Hz timbre band from 0.15 to 0.0006 dB/m — the 7 mm mesh now carries the timbre band the 3.5 mm “Sound” mesh was sold on. On the SAE 2002 rig the station's peak moves 7° toward the measured timing.

What moves, at the 7 mm cell, before → after. The four reference points (El Presidente Tri-Y canon): 2200 rpm 45.51 → 45.45, 2400 46.03 → 46.63, 3200 26.81 → 28.82, 4000 24.07 → 23.76 (drone frequencies unchanged: 110 / 120 / 320 / 400 Hz). The shipped presets: hero 2000 / 3000 / 4000 rpm +2.9 / +12.5 / +7.3 % (the 3000 point 75.8 → 85.3, +1.7 dB), factory −0.2 / +3.6 / −1.2 %, library −0.9 / +1.5 / +6.0 %. the ITB synth +2.1 / +6.7 / +9.1 %, the plenum synth +1.3 / +6.2 / +6.5 %, the post-cat synth −2.3 / +5.2 / +1.6 %, the two-face synth +3.3 / +6.0 / +0.4 %. the two SAE 2002 rigs −2.3 / −1.5 %. documents on a coarse 28 mm mesh +7.5 … +13.5 %. Nine near-tie points relabel their dominant drone bin (hero and ITB at 4000: 400 → 200 Hz. the plenum and the run150 synth at 2000: 200 → 100. the 28 mm rigs at 6000: 300 → 600). At 3.5 mm the moves are the same size or smaller, except the tuned hero 3000 point (+13.5 %), where the old scheme's loss was largest. Nothing diverged and no cell timed out on 77 document-points across both schemes.

The cost. About 1.5× per step at 7 mm on a header document, so a sweep takes about 1.5× longer at the working mesh. a single straight pipe with few junctions pays more (the kernel itself is about 4×). The 7 mm answer is still far cheaper than the old scheme's 3.5 mm answer for a smaller error.

The opt-out. "scheme": "maccormack" at the preset root restores 0.4.10's numbers bit for bit (the old scheme is still in the app, untouched). "weno3" is the cheaper third-order variant. Under the old scheme the tvdDissipation, tvdLimiter, tvbM and dissipationGhostRefresh keys mean what they meant. under the default they are inert. The stored default stays empty — no document gains a key.

One thing the sharper solver stopped hiding. A heated pipe with no loss at all — no wall friction, no damping — can ring: a standing wave builds up and keeps growing, and the old scheme's own numerical damping was what held it down. Real documents have wall friction and do not run lossless. if a document of yours ever rings where it did not before, the linearDamping: kirchhoff opt-in below is the physical term that settles it, and the old scheme is one key away.

New, opt-in: a sharper limiter for the old scheme. Under "scheme": "maccormack", the "tvdLimiter": "tvb" key at the top level of the document tells the Davis limiter to leave a resolved crest alone and keep its full strength only at a genuine jump. an optional "tvbM" (default 40) sets how flat a wave has to be to count as smooth. Off by default and inert under the new default scheme: the reference page for the form is not in the library yet, the answer depends on tvbM at the working mesh (the reference engine's 3200 rpm point reads 26.8 / 27.1 / 27.8 / 28.3 at tvbM 20 / 40 / 80 / 160), and it acts only at coarse cells. Remove the key and the bytes are identical.

New, opt-in: linear pipe damping. Until now the only loss a pipe had was wall friction, which grows with the square of the gas speed and so does almost nothing to the quiet standing wave that rings in a tuned pipe while the valve is shut. Real pipes damp that wave through the thin viscous and thermal layers at the wall — a loss that is linear in the wave (Kirchhoff, 1868. the form is off Ingard & Singhal's page in the library). The new "linearDamping" key on a pipe segment adds it: {"mode": "kirchhoff"} sets the strength from the pipe's bore, its gas and its own fundamental (a valve-side primary rings closed–open, everything else open–open), an optional "frequencyHz" evaluates it at a frequency you name, {"mode": "manual", "coefficient": k} sets the strength directly in 1/s, and {"mode": "off"} is the same as no key. Put it on any primary, secondary, collector or tailpipe segment. the muffler core keeps its own damping and the intake does not read it. It damps the wave only — the mean flow keeps the friction loss it already had and gains nothing. A tuned point moves most: with the key on every segment at 7 mm (measured on the previous scheme) the hero preset's 3000 rpm point read 45.6 where it read 75.8 (−40 %, −10.7 dB), and the four reference points moved −1.9 / −5.6 / −14.9 / +49 %. Off by default because the measurement that would have made it the default did not pass: on the published YZ426 pipe the over-rung standing wave shrinks as the damping says it should and the blowdown pulse correlates better with the measurement, but the closed-valve part of the trace stays out of phase at every strength tried — that phase is set by how hot the gas is when it leaves the cylinder, not by any pipe loss, and a cooler cylinder seed is the next physics item. Remove the key and the bytes are identical.

Note. A tailpipe entered shorter than 50 mm is simulated at 50 mm (the layout floors its last piece). Nothing changes in this release. the SAE 2002 test rig, which had run 50 mm long because of it, now carries the paper's pipe and its pins were re-frozen.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.10
item.description:
Read this first: every pipe is now simulated at the length you entered, and every number on every document with a pipe in it moves. Until this release the solver ran each pipe 1.5 cells shorter than its entered length — 10.5 mm per pipe at the 7 mm cell, and the same fraction of a cell at any cell size. A 6→2→1 header's main path from port to tailpipe lost about 50 mm of 1 400. The wave timing that sets scavenging and drone depends on those lengths, so the fix moves scavenging, drone level and, where two harmonics were close, the reported drone tone, in both directions, on every document — the intake side included. The sizes are below so nothing surprises you. There is no opt-out: a pipe that is not the length you entered is a wrong answer, not an option.

Pipes are their entered length. The 1-D solver builds each pipe from a row of cells with one extra cell at each end that carries the boundary (the valve, a junction, the open end). The cell spacing was set as if the pipe spanned all of those cells, but the boundaries act one and a half cells inside that span, so the pipe the waves saw was 1.5 cells short. The spacing is now set so the boundaries sit exactly the entered length apart. The cell count stays what it was to within one cell, cell size moves by under 1 %, and a run takes 0.7–0.9 % fewer steps.

What it does to the reference points (El Presidente Tri-Y canon, 7 mm cell), before → after. 2200 rpm: scavenging 47.5 → 45.5 (−4.2 %), drone 101.6 → 100.5 dB (−1.0 dB). 2400 rpm: 47.3 → 46.0 (−2.6 %), 102.5 → 101.6 dB (−0.9 dB). 3200 rpm: 24.5 → 26.8 (+9.6 %), 111.1 → 108.6 dB (−2.5 dB). 4000 rpm: 21.3 → 24.1 (+12.9 %), 103.3 → 104.7 dB (+1.4 dB). The drone tone at all four reference points is unchanged (110 / 120 / 320 / 400 Hz). With the pipes short, the canon's answer at 4000 rpm kept moving every time the cell was halved and never settled; with the pipes at their entered length the 7 mm answer is within 1 % of the fine-mesh answer instead of 11 % away.

The shipped presets at the 7 mm cell, before → after. El Presidente as shipped: 2000 rpm 48.8 → 46.0 (−5.7 %, −0.7 dB); 3000 rpm 18.9 → 19.4 (+2.5 %, −1.5 dB); 4000 rpm 21.9 → 24.7 (+13.2 %, +0.8 dB). The BMW M30B35 library engine: 2000 rpm 59.9 → 57.7 (−3.7 %, −0.8 dB); 3000 rpm 30.1 → 27.8 (−7.5 %) and its drone reads 108.3 dB at 150 Hz where it read 114.2 dB at 300 Hz — the 300 Hz label was a 7 mm artefact that the finer meshes never showed, and it is gone at the working mesh now; 4000 rpm 16.2 → 16.5 (+2.0 %, −0.6 dB) with the reported tone moving 200 → 400 Hz (two harmonics of near-equal level; which one is reported can change with the mesh at this point, as it did before). The 6→2→1 hero shape: 2000 rpm 18.0 → 14.7 (−18 %, −1.0 dB); 3000 rpm 70.8 → 75.8 (+7.1 %, +3.5 dB); 4000 rpm 12.7 → 11.8 (−6.9 %, −3.2 dB). At the 3.5 mm cell every one of those moves is about half as large, which is what a 1.5-cell correction does. Coarse documents move the most: at a 28 mm cell the correction is 42 mm per pipe, and a test rig at that cell moved by up to +81 %.

Intake documents. Intake runners and plenums are pipes too and were short by the same 1.5 cells. The ITB and plenum documents read 14–17 % less scavenging at 2000 rpm and about 1 dB less drone. The El Presidente ITB document at 2000 rpm reads 41.2 (was 42.7, −3.5 %).

What does NOT change. The drone tone at every canon reference point. Every explicit setting you have made. No document gains a key. The energy-equation default (ON since 0.4.9) and its per-junction opt-out are untouched. The time-step guard is untouched. What is still not exact: the boundary cell still takes its pressure from the cell next to it, and a junction still builds its face from the first interior cell. Those are smaller mesh effects of the same first-order kind and they are named for the next accuracy pass. At 3200 rpm they still move the canon by about 4 % between the 7 mm and 3.5 mm cells (it was 9 %).

New, opt-in: a header pipe can carry a bend. A primary, secondary or collector segment accepts an inlineBend key (angleDeg, optional clrMm) in the project file and pays the same bend pressure loss the tailpipe chain's bend element already pays (the Idelchik loss from angle, centreline radius and bore, spread along the segment). There is no Inspector row yet. Without the key nothing changes: every existing document computes the same bytes. Measured on the SAE 2002-01-0002 pressure-trace rig, a bend of the printed size moves the station trace by 0.1 %, so it is not the missing dissipation on that rig.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.9
item.description:
Read this first: numbers move on every document that has a merge. This release corrects two things about how a junction reads its own flow and turns one energy option on by default. Every collector, Y-pipe, tee and plenum computes differently now, in both directions, and the drone gets louder at the reference points. The sizes are below so nothing surprises you. Documents whose junctions never see a reversal alongside a live feed, and every explicit setting you have made, are unchanged.

Merge junctions now decide, face by face, which pipe's gas is at each face. The solver used to make one decision for the whole junction: if the total flow was inward it called the junction a merge and gave every face the incoming runners' gas, so a runner blowing back into the junction was filled with a neighbour's gas instead of its own, and the collector was left out of the mixture. Each face is now asked which way its own gas moves. At the 7 mm working cell this alone reads, for the shipped El Presidente Tri-Y, −0.6 % scavenging at 2000 rpm, −7.3 % at 3000 and +16.9 % at 4000; for the BMW M30B35 library shape −1.3 % / +1.4 % / +1.7 %; and for a 6→2→1 header at its torque peak scavenging more than doubles at 3000 rpm (+139 %) with the drone +7.3 dB — that is the case the fix was diagnosed on. A plenum document at 7 mm and 2000 rpm that used to stop solving part-way now completes. A clean forward merge and a full reversal compute exactly what they did before, bit for bit.

Junctions now conserve energy across their faces by default (energyEquation ON). Every face that receives gas carries the mass-averaged stagnation enthalpy of the flows feeding it (SAE 2003-01-0370 eqs 36–39), instead of an imposed entropy label. On top of the face-by-face change, at 7 mm: El Presidente −0.2 % / +2.4 % / +12.3 % scavenging at 2000 / 3000 / 4000 rpm with the drone +0.8 / +1.5 / +1.5 dB; the library shape +1.3 % / +5.3 % / −2.8 %, drone +0.2 / +7.3 / +2.1 dB (its 3000 rpm tone moves 150 → 300 Hz at 7 and 3.5 mm and returns to 150 Hz on a fine cell); the 6→2→1 header +1.9 % / +0.3 % / +15.6 %, drone +0.4 / +0.4 / −0.4 dB. The reference goldens move +6.9 / +10.4 / −9.6 / +7.8 % scavenging and +1.9 / +2.6 / +1.7 / +0.9 dB at 2200 / 2400 / 3200 / 4000 rpm. The large top-end moves are mostly the old closure still travelling under mesh refinement while the new one has settled. Drone tones stay on the same bin at every reference point and solve time is unchanged. To keep the old closure on a junction, set "energyEquation": false on that junction's entry (header.<junction>) in the project file; that restores the 0.4.8 behaviour at that junction bit for bit. No app control yet.

The pipe-end conservation fix from 0.4.8 (dissipationGhostRefresh) is now ON by default. The built-in presets as shipped, the reference goldens and any document whose tailpipe end radiates move nothing, byte for byte. Documents with a non-radiating open end move by up to −2.5 % scavenging / 0.36 dB, and documents with the 1-D resonator branch by up to −6.8 % / −1.8 dB at 2000 rpm at 7 mm (both shrink hard when the cell is halved — the old scheme's mesh error, not new physics). "dissipationGhostRefresh": false in the project file restores the 0.4.8 scheme bit for bit.

Individual-throttle-body intakes no longer stall the solver at low rpm, and their numbers change. The formula for the air at an open runner mouth had no answer once the runner gas was warmer than the outside air and fell through to a formula written for the far end of a pipe, which pushed gas OUT during the intake stroke and fed on itself until the time step collapsed. A 40 mm × 300 mm ITB tract at 7 mm and 2000 rpm used to burn its whole 300-second budget with no answer; it now finishes in 13 seconds. Every ITB document moves, not all one way: on the reference tract +10.8 % scavenging at 3000 rpm and −7.3 % / −1.2 dB at 4000 at 7 mm; El Presidente with the stock ITB tract at 2000 rpm +0.4 % / +0.27 dB. There is no opt-out — the old behaviour was a sign error. Documents with no intake tract and every plenum intake are unchanged byte for byte.

A document whose time step collapses now stops in seconds and names the element. It used to run to its time budget and say “timed out”. The solver now stops the point the moment one element's step falls under what its own mesh allows (a cell claiming gas signalling faster than 25 km/s), returns DIVERGED, and the badge, the saved document, the live-state export and the batch output carry a note naming the step, the element, the cell and its state. On a clean document the guard is a bystander — verified on 47 points through two builds, byte for byte.

The reference golden still reads at the 7 mm working cell. Moving it to a finer cell, where the number pins the model rather than the mesh, was measured and cannot be done inside any test budget: the top-end reference point has not settled to under 1 % per halving even at 0.44 mm, and one point at 0.875 mm already costs about two hours in the test host. If you care about absolute numbers at the top of the rev range rather than about comparing designs, refine the cell. Also in the suite: the first trace comparison on published pipe geometry (SAE 2002-01-0002), which shows the open pipe under-damps at about twice the measured amplitude — recorded, not tuned.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.8
item.description:
The Pressure Field's animation and field snapshots showed pressures up to ~10 % low wherever the gas had cooled. Since 0.4.6 the solver runs a per-cell γ(T), but the within-cycle frames, the six-wire snapshot, the representative field and the travelling-wave base state were still read with the single run γ, so a cell that had cooled toward the wall temperature was under-read. Every frame and field value is now read with the γ the solver wrote that cell with. No solve result changes: sweeps, goldens, scavenging/SPL/drone/brake-power numbers and exports are bit-identical — only what the Pressure Field draws moves, and only on cooled gas.

The algebraic check and simulation readouts now show the gas the solver ran. The Algebraic Check's megaphone cutoff, resonator sound speed and TL panel, the inspector's resolved bandwidth, analytic fH / tuned rpm and peak TL, the Live Rev modal resonator bank and the pressure-field wave split all read the same burned-gas pair the solve does — one number feeds both. On a default document the readouts shift about 0.3 % (the 7 mm resolved bandwidth reads ≈397 Hz instead of ≈398 Hz). No solve result changes.

Gas Properties inspector: three new rows. Burned gas γ / R is a read-only readout of the pair the exhaust solver actually runs. λ (lambda) authors the burn's air/fuel ratio over stoichiometric; the accepted range is 0.680–2.0 and a value outside it is refused with the number, never silently clamped. Per-cell γ(T) is a three-way picker — Default (on), On (explicit), Off — where Default writes nothing to the document. The old γ and R rows stay, relabelled γ (fresh charge) / R (fresh charge): they feed only the throttle-plate manifold ratio and the closed-cycle trapped charge. No solve result changes.

Two new opt-in keys, both off unless you set them. "dissipationGhostRefresh": true fixes a small conservation leak at every pipe end in the smoothing stage (a closed 1 m pipe loses 43× / 22× less energy / mass in 2 000 steps); absent, every result is byte-identical, and on the built-in presets as shipped the key changes nothing. "wallThermal": {"hgTrans": 2.625} scales the gas-side heat-transfer coefficient inside the wall-thermal model (the literature's typical HGTRANS); it is a LARGE lever — up to +11 / +24 scavenging points on the two presets with wall thermal on — so treat it as a sensitivity band until a thermocouple gives your header its own number. Absent key ⇒ nothing changes.

The opt-in junction energy equation (energyEquation, still off by default) now treats a back-flowing collector or secondary as the gas it actually is. Documents that never opted in compute the exact same numbers as before, bit for bit. Also added: the first comparison against a measured exhaust-pipe pressure trace (SAE 2004-32-0007) as a characterization rig in the test suite, and a package test that pins the full-chain low-rpm energy-equation run.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.7
item.description:
Bend heat transfer is now on by default for documents that use the wall-thermal model. If your document opts into wallThermal and its tailpipe chain carries bends, each bend now cools the gas the way a real curved tube does (a curved-pipe enhancement on the wall heat transfer, from Frank's 1986 correlation) instead of behaving like a straight run. What moves: on a chain with authored bends, scavenging reads a little higher — between +0.25 and +0.97 points at eleven of twelve measured points (7 mm mesh, two engines, six speeds; the twelfth reads −0.42), shrinking as the mesh refines — while drone level moves under 0.3 dB with no harmonic re-labels. Documents with no bends in the chain, and every document that never opted into the wall-thermal model, compute the exact same numbers as before, bit for bit. To keep the old straight-pipe behaviour on a bends document, set "curvature": false inside its wallThermal spec.

The opt-in junction energy equation no longer hangs at low rpm. energyEquation stays off by default and nothing changes for documents that never opted in — those compute the exact same numbers as before, bit for bit. If you had hand-set "energyEquation": true on a junction, a 2000 rpm point could grind for minutes and time out. The receiving face at a merge now keeps the arriving branch's own wave and gas state and lets the mixed gas carry the enthalpy behind it, and every such point finishes in the same step count as the flag-off run. Opted-in numbers move (this is a repaired model, not a re-tuned one); flag-off numbers do not.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.6
item.description:
The burned-gas model is now on by default — saved documents' numbers move on this update. Documents that never chose a gas model now run burned-exhaust-mixture gas physics end to end: gas properties follow the actual burned mixture, and inside every pipe they follow the local temperature instead of one hand-picked constant. Measured across four engines at 24 operating points: scavenging typically eases a few percent (median ≈ 5%), drone level usually moves under 1.5 dB, and at a few points the drone's dominant harmonic re-labels where two lines sat within a dB. Documents that chose their gas model explicitly do not move. This lands once, as one re-baseline — the price of the gas being right.

One Collector section again. Collector clocking lives inside the collector it clocks: on a split plan each bank's collector cell carries its own ring, and on a single-pipe plan the ring sits inside the Collector section. The separate "Collector Clocking" section is gone — and so is the wrong-face whole-engine ring that split plans drew inside the final collector.

Clocking ports now pass each other cleanly. While you drag, the other ports hold still and the dragged one follows your pointer straight through them. Release on a free angle and it lands there exactly; release on top of another port and it lands beside it on the nearest free angle. No port ever moves except by your own hand.

Delete everything, start from scratch. All primaries and the secondaries can now be removed, and a new "Delete everything…" control (it asks first) empties the whole build in one step. An emptied document shows the blank page, never a pile of faults.

Brake power and BMEP on sweep results (opt-in). Give a document an fmep spec and Wiebe combustion and every sweep point reports brake power (kW) and BMEP (bar) — with every simplification behind the number disclosed alongside it. Without those keys the fields simply stay absent.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.4
item.description:
Auto-bend no longer destroys a hand-routed run. Dragging a pipe that turns the run splices the new bend into your routing — the tail keeps its shape and simply follows the bend you can actually buy.

Your bend orientation is yours. Once you set a bend's Turn (left/right), nothing the app does — dragging the angle, recomputing the route — can flip it back. A freshly minted bend can still be aimed to either side until you set its Turn: the app helps until you enter the value, then keeps its hands off.

Bend angles snap to the ladder. A drag-made bend lands on a real part angle (7.5° up to 90°); wobbles under 3.75° stay wobbles. A snap toggle turns the measured angle back on.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.3
item.description:
Pipe wall roughness. Every pipe can carry a wall-roughness height ε (mm) — the new Roughness field beside the Friction Factor. 0 = hydraulically smooth; new mild-steel tube ≈ 0.045 mm. It never changes your steady Friction Factor.

Unsteady wall friction, the real kind (opt-in, off by default). The solver can now model the memory of wall shear — the extra drag right after a flow reversal that a constant friction factor cannot see — using the Vardy-Brown turbulent weighting function: smooth-pipe form, or rough-pipe form when the pipe carries a roughness. With the flag off, every existing document computes bit-identical results to 0.4.2.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.2
item.description: Auto-bend materialize: a drag that turns the run now mints a real bend into the document, with its angle, CLR and derived arc length. The solver no longer treats a turned run as straight.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.1
item.description:
0.4.1 — a display fix, and two pieces of physics riding along switched off

The TVD dissipation toggle was lying to you. It displayed OFF while the solver ran it ON, for any project that had never explicitly set it. The toggle now shows what actually runs. No simulation result changes — the solver was always doing the right thing; only the checkbox was wrong.

Also aboard, switched off by default: per-cell temperature-dependent gamma in the flux kernel, and CFTRANS unsteady friction. Both are being checked against measured data before they become defaults. Your existing simulations produce identical numbers to 0.4.0.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.4.0
item.description:
0.4.0 — your existing simulations will read slightly differently after this update

Every release before this one told you your existing simulations produce identical numbers. This one cannot, and that is the point of it.

Exhaustism now uses the paper's corrected joining angle at merge junctions, and its measured separating coefficients when flow reverses through a junction. Both were already in the app, switched off, while they were checked against measured test data. They are on by default now.

What this means for a design you already have. Open it and the numbers will have shifted a little. On the El Presidente reference header:

  • Scavenging moved between +0.6 % and +1.0 % at 2200, 2400 and 3200 rpm, and −7.8 % at 4000 rpm.
  • Drone level moved by 0.5 dB or less at every point — the largest single move was −0.51 dB at 2200 rpm.
  • Drone frequency did not move at all. Every tone stayed on the same frequency, on this header and on every other one tested.

The 4000 rpm point is the big one, and it moves down. At the top of the tuned band the resonator tee takes the hardest hit of reversed flow, and the old model charged nothing for it. The new one charges what the measurements say it costs. That scavenging was never really there.

Nothing changed for junctions you never opted in to the directional model. If a junction is not running directional losses, its numbers are identical.

You can put the old behaviour back, one junction at a time. Set that junction's directional angle correction and separating coefficients to false explicitly and it returns to exactly what it did in 0.3.9.

This is why the version went to 0.4.0 rather than 0.3.10.

1110 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.9
item.description:
0.3.9 — the physics groundwork, all of it switched off by default

Everything below is new capability sitting behind switches that are off. Your saved files open unchanged and your existing simulations produce identical numbers. Nothing here changes an answer you already have.

  • The pane can now build shapes the app could not describe before. Add a merge stage, a cross-link, or a re-split from the Header topology menu — 8-4-2-1, true duals with an H-pipe, a 2-into-1-into-2. Each is removable from its own row, and removing it restores the original file exactly. A shape that cannot work is refused with the reason, and a shape the physics model does not cover yet is refused per node instead of quietly approximated.
  • Junctions read the shape you actually built. How many branches meet, and at what angles, comes from the build's own structure rather than a fixed built-in list.
  • Exhaust gas is now describable as gas, not as a constant. The app can compute gas properties of real burned mixture from composition and temperature instead of one hand-picked number. Off by default.
  • Pipe walls can shed heat the way real pipes do — pulsing about five times harder during blowdown than at cruise, instead of a flat rate. Off by default.
  • The solver now proves its own arithmetic. Six analytic checks run against known exact answers — a textbook shock-tube solution and manufactured solutions with a measured order of accuracy. They run as a gate, so a build that quietly gets worse at maths cannot ship.
  • A headless batch runner. Whole sweeps run from a text file and produce diffable results, with running in parallel proven to give bit-identical numbers to running in sequence.
  • A calibration engine that reports what it cannot know. It fits coefficients to measured data and tells you which knobs the data genuinely constrains, rather than quoting confidence on knobs it could not see. Proven on synthetic data only — no real engine data has been used, and it says so every time it runs.

Solver defaults untouched. 1105 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.8
item.description:
0.3.8 — Deleting a part stops redrawing your work

  • Removing one part no longer reseeds the route. Delete an element and the build simply closes the gap. Everything you drew and positioned around it stays exactly where you put it — nothing is regenerated behind you.
  • Junctions now read the shape you actually built. How many branches meet at a junction, and at what angles, comes from the build's own structure instead of a fixed built-in list. Three-into-one, four-into-one and merged pairs behave exactly as before, and layouts beyond those three now feed the solver correctly. Your saved files are unchanged.

Solver defaults untouched — existing simulations produce identical numbers. 1070 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.7
item.description:
0.3.7 — Nothing changes your numbers but you

  • Every automatic change of an orientation or a value is gone. The engine block no longer deflects a drag — a pipe dragged into it turns red so you can decide, and nothing moves your pipe for you. Finishing a drag writes exactly what that gesture means: a pipe drag its own length, a bend drag its own angle, a slide its two neighbouring pipe lengths. Nothing else is ever rewritten — bend angles commit exactly as you drag or type them.
  • Junction physics: the reverse-flow model now carries the hot common gas into receiving branches (the published model's own energy equation). Off by default — your results are unchanged until you opt in; the shock-tube validation still lands within 0.07 bar of the published experiment.

Solver defaults untouched — existing simulations produce identical numbers. 1053 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.6
item.description:
0.3.6 — The graph underneath, and junction physics proven against a published experiment

  • Exhaust Designer routing: inline parts (resonators, mufflers) now sit on the block face with routes drawn around them, and new parts are added at the end of the part before. A header ending at two exits offers the road back to a single collector as its own row.
  • The header topology is now a real graph under the hood — six primitives instead of a fixed list. Nothing about your files changes (saves are byte-identical); this is the foundation for layouts beyond the three presets.
  • Junction physics, completed and validated: the Bassett directional loss model now covers reverse flow through a junction, applied the way the source paper's own boundary model does. The full set reproduces a published shock-tube experiment (a 1.7 pressure-ratio shock into a 90° tee) within 0.07 bar on all three legs. Off by default — your results are unchanged until you opt in.

Solver defaults untouched — existing simulations produce identical numbers. 1052 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.5
item.description:
0.3.5 — Edit a part where you are looking at it

  • Double-click any part on the Exhaust Designer canvas. A small pane opens on the part itself with its own fields — length, diameter, and whatever else that kind of part has. It is the same set of fields as the settings column, wired to the same numbers, so you can type into whichever one you happen to be looking at and the other follows immediately.
  • Warnings stopped eating the settings column. Each one is now a small orange triangle. Hover it and you get the full text, word for word — nothing was shortened, and nothing changed about when a warning appears.

No solver changes. Your simulation results are untouched. 1002 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.4
item.description:
0.3.4 — Put the collector where you want it

  • The collector can be placed. It used to be pinned to one spot the geometry chose for it — the one part you position by eye on a real car was the one part the drawing would not let you move. Drag it on the Exhaust Designer canvas, or type an exact position into the new Place fields in the Collector settings. A Recentre button puts it back.
  • The primaries re-aim and keep the lengths you authored. Moving the collector changes the angle the runners arrive at, never the length you cut. The run downstream follows the collector's exit, so nothing detaches from it.
  • Your simulation results do not change. This is where the part sits, not what it is — verified against the El Presidente reference, which came back bit-identical.

1002 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.3
item.description:
0.3.3 — Housekeeping

Nothing on screen changes. If you are updating from 0.3.1 or earlier, this release also carries everything in 0.3.2 — the Exhaust Designer fixes and the display units that finally stick.

  • The app is called Exhaustism throughout now. It has been called Exhaustism since July, but the project, the build target and the program file inside the app still carried the working name it was given before it had a real one. They do not any more.
  • Your documents, settings and licence are untouched. The identity macOS uses to recognise the app never changed, so nothing had to be re-registered or re-entered.

No solver changes. 987 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.2
item.description:
0.3.2 — The Designer draws what you typed

  • A bend now turns the run. Adding a bend used to draw it as a straight length pointing the same way as the pipe before it, so the only way to see the turn was to drag the end point round by hand — and then retype the angle the drag had just destroyed. The angle you type is the turn you see. Two bends compound: 45° then 45° leaves the run at 90°.
  • The drawing stops moving on its own. Retyping a bend angle re-aims the run instead of only stretching it, and the run can no longer swing sideways because a neighbouring length happened to collapse to zero.
  • Your display units stick. Length, Diameters, Temperature and Pressure survive quitting the app. They never did — the Units tab saved nothing, so every launch quietly put you back on mm, OD, kelvin and kPa.
  • Zoom survives an edit. Deleting a part used to throw you back to the whole-car view. The canvas keeps its scale and stays where you were looking.
  • Delete key. Select a part on the canvas and press ⌦ or ⌦⌦ to remove it. Backspace inside a number field still edits the number.
  • Inches read as fractions. A measurement shows as 2-1/2, not 2.5 — the way it goes on the tube. Anything off a sixteenth is marked ≈, so a rounded number never passes for an exact one. You can still type decimals or fractions. The cut and build sheets gained fraction columns beside the decimal ones, so the export still sorts.

No solver changes. Goldens bit-identical; 986 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.1
item.description:
0.3.1 — The glove stops going deaf

  • The control channel no longer lives beside your project. Commands are read from a fixed folder, ~/Library/Application Support/Exhaustism/ipc, whether or not a document is open. It used to be derived from the open project's path, which made external control conditional on having saved a file — silently.
  • The failure that prompted this: renaming the app changed its bundle identifier, which moved the preferences domain, which orphaned the remembered project path. The app then launched with nothing open and ignored every command sent to it for nine days, while reporting a stale snapshot as live state. Nothing was broken. Nothing said so.
  • State and run events are still written next to your project when one is open — that copy is a record belonging with the run evidence. It simply is not the channel any more, so Save As can no longer disconnect anything mid-session.
  • Silence is now reportable. The state export names the folder the app is actually watching, so tooling can say “this app is listening somewhere else” instead of trusting an old file.

No solver changes. Goldens bit-identical; 939 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.0
item.description:
0.3.0 — The audit burn: honest numbers, disclosed fallbacks

  • Design RPM is saved with the design — it was being silently discarded, and the Designer and the Algebraic quick-check each kept a private target (4,500 vs 6,000). One scavengingTargetRPM now, shared by both, persisted. Sound keeps its own separate target — scavenging and sound are different physics at different rpm.
  • Every sweep is stamped with its run conditions — ambient, fuel, throttle and model flags travel with the result and into the CSV export, so two sweeps can be compared honestly after the fact.
  • MCSA ceiling: a preset's measured minimum cross-section area now caps effective valve area. No default is invented — unmeasured presets ship nil and the solver says so. Wide-open goldens are bit-identical to 0.2.1.
  • Fallbacks now disclose themselves: a 6→2 build that solves as a single collector shows a SOLVED AS SINGLE COLLECTOR badge (persisted, exported) instead of quietly answering a different question; merge advice carries a clocking disclosure; plenum advisory added.
  • New diagnostic: intake-port pressure trace per RPM point — the ram sequence is now visible next to the exhaust pulse.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.2.1
item.description:
0.2.1 — Licensing, quality of life, lighter launch

  • License system (offline, no phone-home): install a signed .exhaustlic in Settings ▸ License. The alpha stays soft-gated — nothing locks.
  • Spacebar toggles the pressure-field playhead app-wide, or Live Rev play/stop while that tab is visible.
  • WAV export no longer freezes the app — background synthesis with a real progress bar.
  • Live Rev volume knob, persisted; pure listener gain, the dB numbers never move.
  • Much lighter launch: saved results now load from the project sidecar on demand instead of all at once — typical launch memory drops from ~800 MB to ~220 MB on a large result store. Charts render identically once loaded; project files are unchanged.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.2.0
item.description:
0.2.0 — Part throttle (FEA-1)

  • The throttle is now a real lever, not a hidden slider. New Throttle control in the Intake & Combustion inspector.
  • With the intake model ON: the butterfly is a genuine variable restriction (1−cos θ plate law) feeding each ITB runner — manifold vacuum, trapped mass and the exhaust pulse emerge from the gas dynamics.
  • Without the intake model: an honest manifold-pressure map scales the blowdown seed (documented approximation, help text says which model you get).
  • Live Rev throttle slider restored; part-throttle sweeps supported.
  • New diagnostics: EVO seed pressure and trapped-charge temperature.
  • Wide-open-throttle results are bit-identical to 0.1.1.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.1.1
item.description:
0.1.1

  • Unified Dozo theme across every view.
  • Sound-grade 3.5 mm mesh option (timbre band recovered above 800 Hz).
  • Intake & Combustion inspector (ITB runner + Wiebe closed-cycle).
  • Reverse-cone tip now modeled on full cat/resonator/muffler chains.
  • New sidecar document format: autosave writes ~11 MB instead of 226 MB.
